title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 5.1 House of God

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

The church is God's house, a place of prayer and worship. In this sub-strand you will read Matthew 21:12-14, learn why Jesus cleared the temple, list activities that build up the church, and practise ways of respecting the church as a house of worship.

## Strand 5.0: The Church
Sub-strand 5.1: House of God
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) outline lessons learnt from Matthew 21:12-14
b) participate in church activities to grow spiritually
c) appreciate the church as a house of worship

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why is the church a holy place?

## Core competencies
• Collaboration: the skill of teamwork is portrayed as learners mention ways they serve God in church.

## Values
• Responsibility is exhibited as learners list activities they do in church.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social Cohesion: learners live harmoniously as they interact with each other.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing a song related to serving God.
• English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the scriptures.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 5.0 The Church, Sub-strand 5.1 House of God
• Matthew 21:12-14; 1 Corinthians 14:26

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Jesus clears the temple

LESSON 1: JESUS CLEARS THE TEMPLE
=================================

## What you will learn
• Retell Matthew 21:12-14.
• Outline lessons learnt from the passage about God's house.

Curriculum outcomes: a) outline lessons learnt from Matthew 21:12-14; c) appreciate the church as a house of worship

## Introduction
The church is not an ordinary hall. In Matthew 21:12-14 Jesus entered the temple and showed, by what he did and what he said, that God's house is a house of prayer.

## Notes
### What Matthew 21:12-14 says
Read the passage carefully. These are the events it records.

- Jesus went into the temple of God.
- He drove out all who were buying and selling in the temple.
- He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves.
- He said, "It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer, but you have made it a den of thieves."
- The blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.

The passage does not give the names of the sellers. It does not say how many tables there were. We teach only what it says.

### Lessons learnt
- God's house is a house of prayer. That is the name Jesus used for it.
- Buying and selling had taken over the temple. Jesus stopped it.
- He called what they had made it: a den of thieves. The trade in that place was dishonest and had crowded out prayer.
- Money changing and the selling of doves were happening inside God's house. Jesus overturned those tables and seats because that use of the temple was wrong.
- The temple was also a place of mercy. After clearing it, Jesus healed the blind and the lame who came to him there.
- We should not treat the church as a market, a playground or a place for cheating.

### The church as a house of worship
Christians call the church the house of God because it is where his people gather to pray, to hear his word and to worship him. Respecting it means we agree with Jesus: this house is for prayer. We appreciate it when we come to worship God, not to disturb others or to misuse the place.

A quiet heart, a prayer and careful behaviour are ways of saying, "This is God's house."

## Key words
• temple — in this passage, the house of God in Jerusalem where people came to pray
• house of prayer — Jesus' name for God's house, a place set apart for prayer
• den of thieves — the name Jesus used when the temple was turned into a place of cheating

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner says Jesus drove the sellers out because he did not want blind people in the temple. What does Matthew 21:12-14 actually say?

Working:
1. Jesus drove out the buyers and sellers and overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves.
2. He said the house was to be a house of prayer, not a den of thieves.
3. Verse 14 says the blind and the lame came to him in the temple and he healed them.

Answer: He cleared the traders. He welcomed and healed the blind and the lame.

## Activity: Lessons from Matthew 21:12-13
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read Matthew 21:12-14 aloud, one verse at a time.
2. List the lessons learnt from the Bible text.
3. In pairs, list ways of respecting the church as a house of God, using the idea of a house of prayer.
4. Each learner writes one sentence: "The church is a house of prayer because..."

## Practice
1. What did Jesus do to the buyers, the sellers, the money changers and those who sold doves?
2. What name did Jesus give God's house, and what did he say the traders had made it?
3. What happened to the blind and the lame in Matthew 21:14?
4. Give two lessons Christians learn from Matthew 21:12-14.

## Summary
• Jesus drove traders out of the temple and called it a house of prayer.
• He healed the blind and the lame who came to him there.
• The church is to be respected as a house of worship, not misused.

### Answers to practice
1. He drove out those who were buying and selling, and he overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves.
2. He said, "My house shall be called the house of prayer," but they had made it a den of thieves.
3. They came to Jesus in the temple, and he healed them.
4. Any two: God's house is a house of prayer; it must not be used for cheating or as a market; Jesus healed the blind and the lame there; we should respect the church.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Serving and respecting God's house

LESSON 2: SERVING AND RESPECTING GOD'S HOUSE
============================================

## What you will learn
• List church activities that help a Christian grow spiritually.
• Describe ways of respecting the church.

Curriculum outcomes: b) participate in church activities to grow spiritually; c) appreciate the church as a house of worship

## Introduction
People do not only sit in church. They pray, sing, learn and serve. First Corinthians 14:26 and the life of your own church show activities that help Christians grow, if the church is treated as God's house.

## Notes
### Activities named in 1 Corinthians 14:26
Read the verse and list what it mentions. When believers come together, each one may have:

- a psalm, which is a song of praise
- a doctrine, which is a word of teaching
- a tongue
- a revelation, which is something God has made known
- an interpretation, which explains a message

The verse ends with a rule: let all things be done unto edifying. Edifying means building up. Every activity should help the church grow stronger, not show off and not cause confusion.

### Activities learners do in church
In your church you may take part in some of these:

- Singing hymns and choruses
- Praying
- Reading the Bible or listening to it
- Listening to teaching in Sunday school, Sabbath school or the sermon
- Giving an offering
- Welcoming people
- Helping to sweep or arrange chairs
- Taking part in the children's service

Joining in helps you grow spiritually. You learn who God is, you speak to him, you serve others, and you remember that you belong to his people.

### Ways of respecting the church
Because it is a house of prayer:

- Arrive on time and enter quietly.
- Keep silent during prayer and during the teaching.
- Do not run, shout, eat or play in the church while people are worshipping.
- Do not write on walls, break seats or tear hymn books and Bibles.
- Dress neatly.
- If a phone is nearby, keep it silent.
- Leave the place tidy.
- Use the building for worship and service, not as a market or a place to cheat.

A poem about respect, and a song about serving God, help the class remember these ways after the lesson.

## Key words
• edifying — building up the church so that it grows stronger
• worship — giving God honour in prayer, song and listening to his word
• offering — a gift brought to God in church

## Activity: Church activities and a poem of respect
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read 1 Corinthians 14:26 and list the activities mentioned in the Bible text.
2. In groups, list the activities you do in church.
3. In pairs, list ways of respecting the church as a house of God.
4. Write a short poem about respecting the church, then sing a song related to serving God.

## Practice
1. Name three activities mentioned in 1 Corinthians 14:26.
2. Give three activities you can take part in at church.
3. Why should everything in church be done "unto edifying"?
4. Give three ways of respecting the church as a house of prayer.

## Summary
• 1 Corinthians 14:26 lists song, teaching, revelation, tongue and interpretation, all for building up the church.
• Singing, prayer, learning and service help a learner grow spiritually.
• Respect the church as a house of prayer by quiet, careful behaviour.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: a psalm, a doctrine or teaching, a tongue, a revelation, an interpretation. All must be done to build up the church.
2. Any three, for example singing, praying, listening to teaching, giving an offering, welcoming people, or helping to clean.
3. So that the church is built up and grows stronger, not confused or used for showing off.
4. Any three: arrive on time, keep quiet during prayer and teaching, do not run or eat during worship, do not damage the building or books, dress neatly, and leave the place tidy.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 5.1 HOUSE OF GOD
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. What was being sold in the temple when Jesus entered, according to Matthew 21:12?
   A. Only bread and fish
   B. Doves, and money was being changed
   C. School books
   D. Nothing; the temple was empty

2. Jesus said God's house shall be called:
   A. a den of thieves
   B. the house of prayer
   C. a market
   D. a palace

3. What had the traders made of the temple?
   A. A house of prayer
   B. A den of thieves
   C. A school
   D. A hospital

4. What did Jesus do for the blind and the lame in the temple?
   A. He sent them away
   B. He healed them
   C. He asked them to sell doves
   D. He hid them

5. Which activity is named in 1 Corinthians 14:26?
   A. A psalm
   B. A football match
   C. Selling doves
   D. A journey to Egypt

6. Why should church activities build up the church?

7. Which of these helps a learner grow spiritually?
   A. Shouting during the prayer
   B. Listening to Bible teaching and praying
   C. Writing on the church wall
   D. Running in the aisle during the sermon

8. Which action shows respect for the church as a house of God?
   A. Eating and playing during worship
   B. Keeping quiet and not damaging the seats or books
   C. Buying and selling in the service
   D. Arriving only to meet friends outside

9. Give one lesson from Matthew 21:12-14.

10. Why do Christians call the church a holy place?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 5.1 HOUSE OF GOD
========================================

1. B. Doves, and money was being changed
   Jesus overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves.

2. B. the house of prayer
   He said, "My house shall be called the house of prayer."

3. B. A den of thieves
   Jesus said they had made it a den of thieves.

4. B. He healed them
   Matthew 21:14 says they came to him in the temple and he healed them.

5. A. A psalm
   The verse mentions a psalm, a teaching, a tongue, a revelation and an interpretation.

6. 1 Corinthians 14:26 says all things should be done unto edifying, so that the church grows stronger.
   Edifying means building up.

7. B. Listening to Bible teaching and praying
   Prayer and teaching are church activities that help faith to grow.

8. B. Keeping quiet and not damaging the seats or books
   Quiet, careful behaviour treats the church as a house of prayer.

9. God's house is a house of prayer and should not be made a place of cheating; or, Jesus healed the blind and the lame in the temple.
   Lessons must come from what the passage shows.

10. It is God's house, set apart for prayer and worship, as Jesus taught when he called the temple a house of prayer.
   The church is appreciated as a house of worship.
